questions: Does s-bend finish rate rise above 0.55 at 0.40 kg, or does it fall back toward 0.45 kg levels?
Does steering_oscillation on the s-bend stay under about 0.38 (iteration 10 value 0.36), or does lower mass add jitter?
Does the oval finish stay at 1.00 with max_error near 0.02 m?
Does the total score beat 556.7? If not, the 0.45 kg design should be the final geometry.

intent: Test mass 0.40 kg (the contract minimum) on the iteration 10 design, changing only mass from 0.45 kg. Expected result: s-bend finish rate above 0.55, s-bend max_error at or below 0.05 m, oval finish held at 1.00, and a total score above 556.7. If the oval falls or s-bend oscillation exceeds about 0.43, return mass to 0.45 kg, since that is the best tested value.
learning: Iterations 5 to 10 show that the row (x = ±0.04 m, y = 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints) is near its best. Mass has been the lever that improved the s-bend (0.6 kg to 0.45 kg, score 465.8 to 556.7). The 0.40 kg test checks whether that trend continues to the contract minimum.
rationale: Iteration 10 (mass 0.45 kg, five sensors at x = ±0.04 m, y = 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.095 m) is the best design so far at 556.7, up from 465.8 at mass 0.6 kg. Its oval finish was 1.00 with max_error 0.021 m, and its s-bend finish rose to 0.55 with max_error 0.050 m, well under the 0.06 m off-track limit. Its s-bend steering oscillation was 0.36, under the 0.38 threshold I set for continuing the mass cut. The lighter body is the only change that has helped since iteration 5, and the s-bend failures have mostly disappeared. Following the rule in Robot Integrator's feedback, I take the next step on mass to 0.40 kg, the contract minimum, and keep every other geometry value fixed. Lower mass reduces yaw inertia (mass*(L^2+W^2)/12), which helps the remaining s-bend off-track exits (9 of 20 still leave the track). The risk is slip or jitter at the lowest mass, which the observation request will expose. Because this is the final iteration, I stay with the proven row and wheel track, and I change only mass, a single lever with clear evidence behind it.
